messages:
Laura Chen: FYFY ran a long continuous-batching perf run on stage (kv-cache warm + mixed seq distro). Seeing steady batch-growth and rising workspace high-water, memory footprint creeping even after kv hit-rate stabilizes. logs attached.

Jeff Park: can you paste the top-level numbers? curious how kernel selection behaved during the drift.

Laura Chen: here's the sampled summary from the runtime tracer (10m buckets):
```
time    batch_sz  pad_avg  seq_med  kv_hit  reclaimed_bytes
00:00  32        8.5      96       0.20    1.2G
00:10  36        9.2      96       0.65    2.9G
00:20  40        10.1     96       0.88    3.4G
```
Notice pad_avg climbing with kv_hit rising — suggests KV shadowing is causing more per-seq workspace to be kept live (fragmentation + delayed reuse).

Anika Bose: that matches what i saw in the slab/arena traces. Fragments accumulate because small KV-backed allocations are being pinned to recently-used workspaces; reclaiming them is gated by our watermark policy, so reuse gets delayed across batches.

Samir Rao: quick mitigation idea: introduce a small "soft-reserve" per-seq pool and epoch-based reuse. Soft-reserve keeps tiny short-lived allocations in a hot pool for N batches, then returns them to global free lists in an epoch tick. That should reduce cross-batch fragmentation and lower pad churn.

BenchBot: deployed canary probe (reclaim_threshold 0.7 -> 0.5, epoch_reuse enabled) to 5% of traffic at 02:15. Early metrics (30m): pad-waste -18%, overall GPU resident -9%, OOMs 3->0 in canary. No regressions in throughput.

Laura Chen: nice reduction. one concern: 99p latency tail rose ~3% in canary windows. digging traces shows extra kernel-switch in a handful of sequences when epoch_reuse returns buffers that change preferred kernel variant (small-workspace vs fused-kernel). Kernel-switch cost is small but shows up at 99p.

Jeff Park: interesting tradeoff. Could we prefer reuse that preserves kernel-affinity? e.g., tag buffers with last-used-kernel and prefer returning same-kernel buffers for same seq-shape.

Anika Bose: that's doable; allocator can carry a 1-byte affinity tag. When reusing, prefer matching affinity, fallback to neutral pool. Also schedule a low-priority defrag pass when GPU util < 40% to coalesce tiny slabs into bigger blocks — cost ~= 2-3ms but only runs during idle windows.

Samir Rao: i'll add a perf scenario for this: synthetic seq distro with high kv-density + low-medium seq variance, run 1h and compare mem-watermark, pad-waste, and tail-latency across variants (baseline, soft-reserve, soft-reserve+affinity, +defrag). will push to regression suite.

Laura Chen: thanks. TL;DR: soft-reserve + epoch reuse + lower reclaim threshold cuts padding waste and OOMs. Watch kernel-switch latency at tail; next steps: implement kernel-affinity tags + opportunistic defrag, perf-test, then expand canary. I'll open a tracker and assign tasks. :thumbsup:
